questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since Universitat de Barcelona is a top university in Spain (and nr. 1 in Catalunya), I had big expectations for its academic opportunities. This was well met, as I found the classes, professors and co-students to be of high quality. Therefore, I learned how social economics works in a southern European country, which has been through huge financial crisis'. Otherwise, I chose Barcelona because of its cultural differences from Denmark. I wanted to learn the Catalan culture is significant for the people living in Barcelona, making my stay very local.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The study abroad lived well up to my expectations, as I learned a lot about the culture, economy and myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, it was very difficult getting he right information. It took a long time for the UB to confirm the starting dates of my classes, since I am on the masters degree. For bachelor students it is easier. The communication could have been separated between bachelors and masters students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office was easy to contact, and was good at answering relevant questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. You can look at housing pages such as HousingAnywhere, AirBNB and others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should look into the different neighborhoods before choosing where to stay. They are very different from each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We met at the Erasmus Office and got everything fixed in short time, i.e. registration for courses etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Phone, E-mail and personal help in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Signing up for courses in the Master's degree is no problem. The classes are very small and never filled up, why registrering for courses was not a problem.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of research papers, which makes the full curriculum. It got a bit uniform and boring.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses differs a lot. Some are quite hard, i.e. the macroeconomic courses, however the econometric courses are of low level compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of presentations at UB, which is really great, since at UCPH there are none. 
Otherwise the teaching style is more one-sided at UB, and lacks some student interaction/exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic geography, Empirical approach to economic growth, Macroeconometrics, Microeconometrics, Welfare economics, Economic growth I, International trade.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic growth I was a tough but rich in learning. I can recommend that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I were enrolled in tennis lectures at the University. 40€ for 12 lectures, which were very cheap.
I was dissatisfied that there were parties, such as friday bars or something likewise.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UB-sports, with cheap access to tennis, padel tennis and football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None, I didn't attend to any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the beach, experience the different neighborhoods, bars cafés and local restaurants.
Get local friends, so they can show you the proper city. You can do that through sports, which is easy, as a lot of young persons in Barcelona do sports regularly.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You have to get used to the different "eating periods", where every meal is moved two hours ahead.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Use Celebreak app to play football with randoms and meat friends. 
Go to local bars and reggeaton dancing clubs to meet young locals who also like to go out.
Be openminded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local's can be tough against turists, and they might think you are a turist until you prove them wrong. Why, sometimes it is hard to get local friends/student friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be social in the beginning, as you will create a strong bond to those friends you meet from the beginning.
Don't be affraid to talk with the professors/offices when you are in doubt about anything, they are very helpful.
Come to classes, as it is one of the places where you can meet new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt, call the Erasmus office at the host university in stead of corresponding over E-mail, which can be quite difficult.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: How easy it is to get friends, whether they are danish, swedish, catalan or anything. Culture meets in Barcelona.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting local friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
